unfold.unfolded: Let $S$ be an ordered semigroup, and let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$, where $(X]=\{x\in S : x\le y \text{ for some } y\in X\}$. Then the following hold. (1) $A\subseteq(A]$. (2) $((A]]=(A]$. (3) If $A\subseteq B$ then $(A]\subseteq(B]$. (4) $(A\cap B]\subseteq(A]\cap(B]$. (5) $(A\cup B]=(A]\cup(B]$. (6) $(A](B]\subseteq(AB]$. (7) $((A](B]]=(AB]$.
notes: The closure (X] is not defined in the context; the usual definition is used.

verdict.reason: The unfolded form reproduces all seven statements with the same hypotheses. It only makes the down-set notation $(X]$ explicit.
